sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13644 of 2023
Applicant :- Pawan Kumar

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Vashistha

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Nirbhay Singh
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Heard Sri Ajay Kumar Vashistha, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Nirbhay Singh, learned counsel for the informant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in S.C. No. 905 of 2022, Case Crime No. 585 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 323, 506 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Kasganj, District Kasganj during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown persons under Sections 363, 366 IPC and according to the FIR the minor daughter of the informant aged about 17 years, who was student of class 12th, did not return back to home and it appears that some unknown lad has enticed her away.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant was not named in the FIR and when the statement of victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then she although disclosed the name of applicant but only stated that applicant has taken her to Delhi and thereafter he outraged her modesty and no allegation of rape was made by the victim against the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. but when the statement of victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded after two months then she changed the entire version stated under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and Pawan Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144242941/
1 stated that applicant committed rape with her and this fact clearly suggests that she stated against the applicant under pressure of informant as she up to two months resided in her paternal home.

entities.text: Pawan Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that applicant neither enticed nor abducted the victim nor ever committed rape with her.

5. Per contra, learned AGA and learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that there is specific allegation of rape against applicant in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. but both the counsels could not dispute the fact that in earlier statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she did not make any allegation of rape and further from the date of recording statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. up to the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C victim resided in her paternal home along with her parents.
6.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Although, complicity of applicant was revealed through the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. but in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she did not make any allegation of rape against the applicant and only stated that applicant outraged her modesty but when the statement of victim was recorded after two months under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she stated that applicant committed rape with her.

8. As statement of victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded after two months and in the meantime she resided in her paternal home and earlier in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she did not make any allegation of rape against the applicant

, therefore, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
9. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant - Pawan Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
11. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
